Distinct from stonework:targets: targets is a direct, open-domain/range lift of the STIX 2.1 relationship_type 'targets' shortcut, describing higher-level strategic targeting (a Sector, a Location, an Agent) by a Campaign/MalwareSample/ThreatActor. actsOn is purpose-built for the concrete technical asset one execution-trace Activity acted upon — the same distinction develop draws between stonework:mitigates (open, STIX-lifted) and stonework:mitigatesAttackPattern (purpose-built, controlled domain/range).

definition.value: Relates an entity to an AttackPattern representing the same underlying technique in a different framework shape, resolved from a shared technique identifier (e.g. a CAPEC entry and the MITRE ATT&CK technique it maps to, or a CWE weakness and the CAPEC pattern that exploits it).

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally left unset: subjects include stonework:Weakness (CWE → CAPEC) and stonework:AttackPattern itself (CAPEC → ATT&CK). Materialized by joining a framework's technique-identifier literal (see stonework:relatedTechniqueIdentifier) against the ATT&CK technique's external reference. Framework ontologies declare their concrete property (e.g. capec:relatedAttackTechnique, cwe:relatedAttackPattern) as rdfs:subPropertyOf this.

definition.value: The assessed severity of the incident or event (e.g. critical, high, medium, low, informational).
Relates malware, a product, cyber activity, or agent to infrastructure it uses.

scopeNote.value: Use for an operational dependency on infrastructure, such as malware using command-and-control infrastructure, a CyberActivityCluster or Campaign using hosting infrastructure, a product using a supporting service, or an Agent using infrastructure in an operation. This relationship asserts use, not ownership, compromise, or attribution.

definition.value: Relates a Location to another Location with which it shares a border or boundary, e.g. two neighboring Countries or Regions.

scopeNote.value: Symmetric and not transitive. Use stonework:locatedWithin for containment rather than adjacency.

definition.value: Relates an Infrastructure entity to a contextual record of a product installed on it.

scopeNote.value: Use stonework:hasInstalledProduct for a direct Infrastructure-to-VersionedProduct inventory assertion. Use this property with stonework:installationOf when installation-specific identity, path, licensee, or configuration details must be preserved.

definition.value: Relates a Sighting to the Agent who made the observation.
The most recent timestamp when the entity was observed.

scopeNote.value: Use with stonework:firstSeen to delimit an observation window. For the execution interval of a stonework:CyberActivity, use stonework:startedAtTime and stonework:endedAtTime instead.

definition.value: The CVSS vector string encoding the metric values used to compute the headline base score, e.g. 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H'.
The number of decimal places in the currency's minor unit — 0 for JPY, 2 for USD, 3 for BHD — as defined by ISO 4217 for fiat currencies.
Relates the execution of a Step to the execution of the Plan or Step it is part of.

scopeNote.value: Groups a run's step executions, as a P-Plan bundle groups a plan's execution trace, so that queries over a plan run many times (which steps ran, which were skipped, which values were bound) are asked of one run at a time. Links to the immediate parent only; nested Steps form a chain to the run, which is the execution that is stonework:executionOf the Plan. An execution may be both a Step's execution in one plan and a run of another, as when an investigation's containment Step is carried out by running a ControlPlan: it is then stonework:partOfExecution the investigation, stonework:correspondsToStep the Step, and stonework:executionOf the ControlPlan. Not transitive, so that each execution's parent stays unambiguous; use a SPARQL property path (stonework:partOfExecution+) for every ancestor.

definition.value: The canonical product name.
Relates NetworkTraffic, or an activity observed on the network, to the source IP address: the client of a sign-in, the sending server of a Received hop.

scopeNote.value: Where the address was is a fact about the address: say it with stonework:locatedAt on the IPAddress (a geolocation lookup gives a Country or Region), not on the activity.

definition.value: Indicates two entities have been analytically grouped together based on shared characteristics or behaviour, without implying a stronger semantic relationship.
Generic reference from one entity to another. Use a more specific property where one exists.
The end of the interval during which a qualified assertion is considered applicable.
A CourseOfAction (patch, workaround, compensating control) addresses this Vulnerability. Distinct from stonework:mitigates (Countermeasure → AttackPattern).
The start of the interval during which a qualified assertion is considered applicable.
Relates an AutonomousSystem or IPBlock to an IPAddress or more-specific IPBlock contained within its routed address space.
The version string for this specific product release.
An address in an EmailMessage's Reply-To header, where replies go.

scopeNote.value: A Reply-To that differs from the From address sends the recipient's answer to someone else, a common step in business email compromise. STIX has no Reply-To property.

definition.value: The domestic account number string.
Relates a ThreatScenario to the threat actor type or group it models.
Relates a detection rule to an ordinal assessment of its expected false-positive frequency.
Relates a Host to the NetworkServices it provides.
The Agent that owns or is associated with this EmailAddress. Inverse of stonework:hasEmail.
Relates an Agent to the geographic Location from which it originates.
The date and time at which the vulnerability record was last modified in its source database.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.dateUpdated in CVE JSON 5.x and equivalent update timestamps from other vulnerability sources. cve:dateUpdated is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: A cyber activity that this transaction finances — for example an infrastructure purchase linked to the campaign or operation it supports.

scopeNote.value: This property asserts a financing relationship. For a payment made in response to an activity without financing it, such as a victim's ransom payment made because of an incident, use stonework:respondsToActivity.

definition.value: The display name associated with the email address.
Relates a SecurityActuator to a SecurityActuation it performed.
The payment instrument or rail used to execute this transaction — wire, ACH, SEPA, card, cash, on-chain transfer, and so on.
Convenience projection of the magnitude of a single-denomination transaction's stonework:MonetaryAmount, paired with stonework:transactionCurrency.

scopeNote.value: Do not use for a currency exchange with distinct input and output amounts; use stonework:originatorMonetaryValue and stonework:beneficiaryMonetaryValue instead.

definition.value: Relates an AnalyticTechnique or DefendTechnique to an AITechnique or AttackTechnique it detects, neutralizes, or mitigates.
Relates one Infrastructure entity to another Infrastructure entity to which it resolves, such as a Domain resolving to an IPAddress.
Relates a Directory to the Files it contains.
Relates an AutonomousSystem to an IPBlock it originates or announces.
A File is code-signed with this Certificate. Supports trust chain analysis, publisher attribution of binaries, and detection of certificate abuse or misuse.
Relates a vulnerability to a structured CVSS metric record carrying the version, vector string, and base/temporal/environmental scores.

scopeNote.value: A single vulnerability may carry metrics for multiple CVSS versions (2.0, 3.1, 4.0) or scoring authorities. For a single headline score and severity, use stonework:cvssBaseScore and stonework:cvssSeverity directly on the Vulnerability. Core consumers can represent the common structured fields without an adapter; load the CVSS framework module for decomposed vector components and additional subscores.

definition.value: The TCP/UDP port number on which the service listens.
Relates a Hypothesis to something it is about: a technique, actor, account, asset, vulnerability or event.

scopeNote.value: For finding hypotheses ("everything we've hypothesized about T1114.003", "about the controller's account"), not for judging them. Not functional: "the actor is using a forwarding rule on the controller's mailbox" is about the actor, the technique and the mailbox. The values carry no roles; a claim whose roles matter, or whose parts can fail separately, is split into parts with stonework:hypothesisPart. A compound Hypothesis is also about whatever its parts are about, so it need not repeat them: follow stonework:hypothesisPart* first. Range deliberately unset, like stonework:noteAbout.

definition.value: The scalar value a Hypothesis predicts its stonework:predictsVariable will be bound to, once executed.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors stonework:boundToLiteral on the actual-result side; see stonework:predictedValue for predictions of an individual rather than a scalar.

definition.value: Relates a hash entry to the entity it describes. The domain is a stonework:Hash individual representing a single hash algorithm and digest value.
Relates an Investigation or Incident to how urgently it should be worked.

scopeNote.value: Priority is a decision about ordering work, distinct from stonework:ImpactLevel and stonework:RiskLevel, which assess consequence and likelihood; a high-impact matter may still be a lower priority than another. At most one current priority.

definition.value: An address a MailboxRule redirects the messages it selects to, keeping the original sender, so the recipient sees them as if sent directly.
A PhoneNumber associated with this Agent.
Relates a product to another product that depends on it. Transitive to support supply chain reasoning across deep dependency trees.
Relates an exploitation-report observation to the kind of report it records.

scopeNote.value: At most one per observation (stonework:ExploitationReportKindShape). A source that reports several kinds for one vulnerability records one observation per kind.

definition.value: The timestamp when this individual was last modified.

scopeNote.value: Compatibility alias for dcterms:modified. Prefer dcterms:modified in newly authored data.

definition.value: The size of the file in bytes.
Links a MalwareSample to a captured binary artifact (file, memory dump, or encoded payload) constituting the physical evidence of the sample.

scopeNote.value: Optional — a MalwareSample may be known via hashes or threat reports without the binary being available. When present, the artifact provides retrievable binary evidence. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 sample_refs property on the malware SDO.

definition.value: Relates a Playbook or ThreatScenario to an AttackTechnique, MalwareFamily, or ThreatActor it is designed to address.
Relates an activity (a Process, an Event such as a log record, or any other CyberActivity) to the Agent that performed it, or a Plan to the Agent responsible for carrying it out.

scopeNote.value: On an execution, name the performer as observed. When the evidence shows only an identity, such as an account in an audit log, the performer is that DigitalIdentity, and the Agent behind it is reached through stonework:accountOf or stonework:attributedToAgent. When an identity may have been used by someone other than its holder, keep the identity as the performer and record the Agent believed responsible with stonework:attributedTo; an analyst who establishes the misuse records a stonework:Deviation. Who is expected to perform a Plan's Steps is given per Step, as Roles (stonework:performerRole).

definition.value: The complete vector string used by a structured CVSS assessment.

scopeNote.value: cve:vectorString (on cve:CvssMetric) is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: The system, component, or application that generated the log (e.g. Windows Security, syslog, Apache).
Relates an Investigation to a Hypothesis it tests.

scopeNote.value: The direct link from an Investigation to its Hypotheses. When the Investigation executes an InvestigationPlan, the Hypothesis also predicts a Variable of a Step in that plan (stonework:predictsVariable); its outcome is stonework:hasHypothesisStatus.

definition.value: The MIME type of the file (e.g. application/x-executable, text/html).
The source vocabulary's wire-level name for the relation expressed by a qualified assertion.

scopeNote.value: Preserves open relationship vocabularies such as STIX relationship_type strings. A separately materialized object property may provide a query-friendly projection of the same assertion.

definition.value: Relates a Behavior plan to a CyberActivity that executes it.
Links an enterprise infrastructure to a versioned product known to be installed in that environment.

scopeNote.value: Used in the user-data graph to assert enterprise inventory directly. Combined with stonework:versionOf and stonework:affected, enables traversal from installed software to applicable CVEs. For SBOM-based ingest with full component provenance, see stonework:SoftwareBillOfMaterials and stonework:hasBomEntry.

definition.value: Asserts that when the source Indicator's pattern is matched, it signals the presence of the target adversary behavior, malware, campaign, or threat actor.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'indicates'. Domain is stonework:Indicator — unlike the source side of other STIX relationship shortcuts, this is definitional rather than open-world convention: an object is only ever an Indicator because it indicates something, per STIX's own spec role for that object type. Range is intentionally left unset: an Indicator may indicate all sorts of things (AttackPattern/AttackTechnique, Malware, Campaign, CyberActivityCluster, ThreatActor, Infrastructure, Tool, and whatever else a producer's pattern targets), and STIX does not schema-constrain the target_ref type for a given relationship_type. A single Indicator may indicate multiple targets.

definition.value: A context-free projection of a Role played by an entity.

scopeNote.value: Use stonework:RoleAssignment with stonework:roleContext when the campaign, operation, organization, provenance, or time interval matters. The qualified pattern infers this direct projection through a property chain.

definition.value: The number of times the sighted object was observed.
The Role assigned by a qualified RoleAssignment.
The Step a Transition enters.

scopeNote.value: A Transition whose toStep was already reached earlier in the same Behavior's Step graph expresses a loop back-edge; a self-loop (toStep equal to fromStep) is the degenerate case.

definition.value: Relates a Person to the Organization they work for.
Relates the subject of an Investigation to the Investigation examining it.

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally unset; see stonework:investigates.

definition.value: The address in an EmailMessage's Sender header: the mailbox that sent the message on the author's behalf.
Relates a threat actor to one or more motivations that drive their actions and operations.

scopeNote.value: A threat actor may have multiple motivations. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 primary_motivation and secondary_motivations properties on ThreatActor.

definition.value: A currency or crypto asset that this financial account holds or is denominated in.

scopeNote.value: Intentionally multi-valued: an account, including a hosted exchange account or multi-asset wallet, may hold or support more than one currency.

definition.value: Relates an Event to the Host on which it was observed.
The date the item was first publicly published or disclosed.

scopeNote.value: Compatibility alias for dcterms:issued. Prefer dcterms:issued in newly authored data.

definition.value: Links a digital identity to the real-world Agent it is believed to belong to.

scopeNote.value: Names the identity's holder, not whoever used it on a given occasion. When an identity is used by someone else, such as an actor holding a victim's stolen credentials, the activity keeps the identity as its stonework:performedBy and names the Agent responsible with stonework:attributedTo. That someone else controlled the identity for a period, such as an actor holding a mailbox's credentials from its compromise to its containment, is a stonework:IdentityControl.

definition.value: An address in an EmailMessage's Bcc header, where the sender's copy records one.
The financial institution that maintains this account.

scopeNote.value: Optional. Absent for a self-custody crypto wallet or an account whose institution is unknown; present and pointing at a virtual asset service provider for a custodial wallet.

definition.value: The name of the packer or obfuscator used (e.g. UPX, Themida).
The filesystem path of the process executable image.
Relates a Behavior (Procedure, Playbook, ThreatScenario, Control, or another Step) to a Step that decomposes it.

scopeNote.value: Domain is the general Behavior root rather than a specific subclass, so decomposition applies uniformly across Procedure, Playbook, ThreatScenario, and — recursively, since Step is itself a Behavior — Step.

definition.value: The date and time at which a metric observation was made or calculated.
An authenticator presented in an activity, such as a sign-in.

scopeNote.value: Several for a multifactor sign-in (a password and a push approval). A sign-in that presented a session token rather than authenticating afresh is authenticatedWith stonework:authenticatorSessionToken, with no stonework:authenticationFactor.

definition.value: Relates a Hypothesis to its current status in the confirm/refute lifecycle.

scopeNote.value: Kept explicit (rather than inferred from which Transition fired) so a Hypothesis's status is directly queryable without replaying the Step graph it was tested in.

definition.value: Relates a ThreatScenario to the targeted assets in the scenario.
Generic link between two entities. Use a more specific property where one exists.
The date and time at which a CyberActivity ended.
Relates an AccessControlList to a UserAccount or UserGroup whose permissions it records.
The unique serial number assigned to the certificate by the issuing CA.
An address a MailboxRule forwards the messages it selects to, inline or as attachments.
Relates a product version to an older version it replaces. Transitive to support full product lifecycle reasoning.
The vulnerability evaluated by a structured CVSS assessment.

scopeNote.value: Declared rdfs:subPropertyOf stonework:assessmentOf so a query over assessmentOf returns every Assessment of a Vulnerability — CVSS metrics included — without needing to know each scheme's specific property name.

definition.value: A numeric score (0.0–1.0) representing the estimated probability of occurrence.

scopeNote.value: Convenience projection for a current value. Use stonework:MetricObservation with stonework:metricLikelihoodScore when source, assessment time, or model version must be preserved.

definition.value: The CVE identifier in the format CVE-YYYY-NNNNN.

scopeNote.value: Retained as the STONEWORK-level CVE-specific identifier. cve:cveId (declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property) is the source-native alias always present on data ingested from CVE JSON; query this property for cross-source lookups.

definition.value: The RuntimeProcess that opened this NetworkTraffic flow. Core process-to-network correlation arc for host-based forensics and lateral movement analysis.
A Step of the run's Plan that a Deviation concerns.

scopeNote.value: One Step for a skipped, wrong-role or misused-identity deviation; both Steps for a same-agent or out-of-order one.

definition.value: The Message-ID header of an EmailMessage, with its angle brackets.
A stonework:FinancialAccount that this stonework:UserAccount, a login or credential, can operate.

scopeNote.value: Distinct from stonework:accountOf, which records the holder or beneficial owner. One login often controls several financial accounts; a financial account seen in isolation, such as an IBAN in wire data, may have no associated login. An account-takeover attacker holding a victim's UserAccount controls the victim's FinancialAccount without being its accountOf.

definition.value: Links a CyberActivity to the Agent responsible for, or associated with, performing it.

scopeNote.value: Domain/range intentionally left unset: this property is a direct lift of the STIX 2.1 relationship_type 'attributed-to' shortcut. STIX does not schema-constrain which SDO/SCO types may appear as source_ref/target_ref for a given relationship_type — that's producer convention, not enforceable structure, and a closed domain/range here would misrepresent real STIX 2.1 data and mislead reasoner-based consumers. In practice the object is typically a stonework:Agent — most often a stonework:ThreatActor in the adversarial case, matching STIX's own convention for 'attributed-to' — but stonework:CyberActivity is a general occurrence class covering defensive and neutral activities too (Investigations, a ControlPlan's Process), so the performer need not be adversarial.

definition.value: The postal or ZIP code of the location.
The individual a Variable resolved to in one execution, e.g. the specific SecurityCondition a successful attempt produced.

scopeNote.value: Used when the bound value is an instance of a class rather than a scalar; see stonework:boundToLiteral for scalar bindings. Tested by stonework:guardType on a Transition. Since 0.12.0 the subject is a stonework:VariableBinding, not the Variable, so each execution has its own value.

definition.value: The banner string returned by the service upon connection.
The process identifier assigned by the OS.
Relates a Provenance record to the IntelligenceProduct or QualifiedAssertion whose origin or evidentiary basis it documents.
A brief summary of the intelligence product's key findings.
A File resides in this Directory. Inverse of stonework:containsFile; enables upward traversal of the file system tree.
The qualitative CVSS severity rating corresponding to the headline base score: NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL.
Relates an IPAddress to the AutonomousSystem that originates its encompassing IP prefix in BGP.
The comparison operator applied between guardVariable's bound literal value and guardLiteralValue.

scopeNote.value: Omitted = Equals, preserving equality-only guard semantics without requiring this property on every Transition.

definition.value: A short name identifying a Variable within the scope of its declaring Behavior, allowing it to be referenced consistently across Steps and Transitions.
Relates a Sensor to the Detection Rules it applies.
The name of the registry value.
Relates an entity to a qualified assignment of a Role in a specific context.
The total number of bytes transmitted in the traffic flow.
Relates a concrete, Step-decomposed Behavior to the more abstract Behavior it is a specific realization of.

scopeNote.value: General-purpose relationship covering both offense (a Procedure implements a Technique) and defense (a ControlPlan implements a Control) with one property rather than a bespoke one per pairing.

definition.value: A DigitalArtifact written to the filesystem or memory by this MalwareSample during execution.
Relates an Intelligence Product to the Agent that created it.
Generic composition relationship. Use stonework:consistsOfCampaign or a more specific property where possible.
Relates a MalwareSample or Tool to Infrastructure or a URI with which it exchanges command-and-control or exfiltration traffic. Distinct from stonework:deliveredVia, which covers initial delivery.
Relates a Sighting to the entity that was observed.
The email address string (local@domain).
A Domain resolves to this IPAddress via DNS. More specific than stonework:resolvesTo (Infrastructure → Infrastructure); use this for explicit domain-to-IP mappings.
Relates a component context to the versioned product it references or instantiates.

scopeNote.value: Used by stonework:BomEntry (declarative — a component listed in an SBOM), stonework:ProductInstallation (observational — a verified deployment on a specific system), and other stonework:ComponentContext subclasses. Domain is intentionally left unset to avoid restricting future component-context subclasses. Not declared owl:FunctionalProperty at the property level, because not every ComponentContext subclass is one-to-one with a product — a source-native advisory entry may legitimately name several. BomEntry and ProductInstallation instead carry a local owl:maxQualifiedCardinality 1 restriction on this property (onClass stonework:VersionedProduct), which gives those two classes the same at-most-one guarantee without constraining subclasses that don't share it.

definition.value: The name of the user group.
The Agent associated with this PhoneNumber. Inverse of stonework:hasPhoneNumber.
Relates an Organization or ThreatActor to the Locations or Sectors they operate in.
Relates a product version to another product version it depends on.
An execution in the run that a Deviation concerns, such as the execution performed by the wrong Role.

scopeNote.value: Absent for a skipped Step, which has no execution. Needed when a Step runs more than once in a run, to say which execution deviated.

definition.value: The cryptographic hash algorithm used (e.g. MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SSDEEP).
Relates a Plan to what it is for: attack, detection, engagement, investigation, mitigation, notification, prevention or remediation.

scopeNote.value: Not functional: a Plan may have several types, as a CACAO playbook may. The Plan subclasses already say some of this (see stonework:PlaybookType); the type is stated explicitly, not inferred, because a ControlPlan can be any of three.

definition.value: The version string of the detection rule.
Relates a Host or NetworkService to an IPAddress assigned to or used by it.
The registered name or handle of the autonomous system.
Relates a MalwareFamily or MalwareSample to another family or sample from which it is derived, modified, or evolved, indicating shared code lineage, forked development, or deliberate repackaging.
Relates an Analysis to the CyberEntity or CyberActivity that it examines.
The network or transport protocol (e.g. TCP, UDP, ICMP, HTTP, DNS).
The name of the network service (e.g. HTTP, SSH, RDP, SMB).
The Distinguished Name of the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate.
A description of the strategic goal or objective being pursued.
A RuntimeProcess creates a child process. Inverse of stonework:hasParentProcess; enables top-down process tree traversal for execution chain analysis.
The account debited by this transaction — the source of the transferred value.

scopeNote.value: Naming follows the FATF Travel Rule and ISO 20022 originator-beneficiary convention. Direction of value is carried by these roles, not by the sign of stonework:amount.

definition.value: The geographic latitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84).
How a Step's outgoing Transitions are taken when it finishes: exclusive, exactly one, whose guard holds; parallel, every one whose guard holds, as concurrent branches.

scopeNote.value: Omitted means exclusive, the meaning several outgoing Transitions had before splitKind existed. With parallel, an unguarded Transition is always taken, so a parallel split whose Transitions are all unguarded is BPMN's parallel gateway, and one whose Transitions are guarded is its inclusive gateway. The branches may overlap in time; the Step where they meet says by its stonework:joinKind whether it waits for them all. As in YAWL, a split is a property of the Step it follows, not a separate gateway node, so every Step remains a unit of action; a BPMN diverging gateway maps onto the splitKind of the Step before it.

definition.value: A framework-native technique identifier string (e.g. a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID such as 'T1003.001') carried on an entity from another framework, both for provenance and as the join key used to materialize the corresponding stonework:relatedAttackPattern or stonework:mitigatesAttackPattern edge.

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally left unset: populated on entities as different as capec:AttackPattern and cis:Control. Framework-specific subproperties (e.g. capec:attackTechniqueId, cis:mitigatesTechniqueId) carry the concrete literal. Retained after materialization — it records the source string as ingested, distinct from the resolved object-property edge.

definition.value: A Vulnerability is formally disclosed in this Publication (advisory, CVE NVD entry, security bulletin). Primary arc into the Publication class.
The base score calculated by a structured CVSS assessment, on a 0.0-10.0 scale.

scopeNote.value: cve:baseScore (on cve:CvssMetric) is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: Relates an Investigation to the digital artifacts it collects as evidence.
Relates a Risk to its associated Impact component.
Relates a DataAsset to the Infrastructure system that stores it.
The file extension without the leading dot (e.g. exe, dll, ps1).
The control family or category grouping a control belongs to, by code or name (e.g. AC or Access Control, IR or Incident Response).

scopeNote.value: nist:family, the two-letter NIST SP 800-53 family code, is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property.

definition.value: Relates an Assessment to the entity being assessed.

scopeNote.value: Scheme-specific linking properties, such as stonework:cvssMetricFor, are declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property, so a query over assessmentOf reaches every Assessment subclass regardless of scheme.

definition.value: Declares a Variable whose value must be bound before the Behavior or Step executes.
The date and time when the domain was first registered.

scopeNote.value: Uses xsd:dateTime so source-native registration timestamps, including dns:registeredOn, can map without losing precision.

definition.value: Relates an Investigation to an intelligence product it considers as a source, such as a Report, a vendor's threat bulletin, or an imported STIX bundle.

scopeNote.value: The intelligence-side counterpart of stonework:collects, which is for the DigitalArtifacts an Investigation collects as forensic evidence. What an Investigation produces is stonework:producesReport.

definition.value: Relates a Tactic to a Technique that serves its goal, or a Technique to a more specific Technique it contains.
Links a Software Bill of Materials to the enterprise infrastructure, system, or application whose component composition it inventories.

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally left unset. The primary subject is stonework:SoftwareBillOfMaterials, but other provenance-bearing artifacts may describe infrastructure without being SBOMs. Multiple SBOMs may describe the same Infrastructure over time, enabling historical component inventory.

definition.value: Relates a Countermeasure or ACL to the resource it protects.
The machine-readable format a Plan is also kept in, e.g. CACAO JSON for a playbook or BPMN for a business process.
Relates an entity to its physical or logical location.
The date and time at which a vulnerability identifier was assigned by the relevant numbering authority.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.dateReserved in CVE JSON 5.x and equivalent assignment timestamps from other vulnerability sources. cve:dateAssigned is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: The outgoing Transition a Step takes when no other outgoing Transition's guard holds.

scopeNote.value: BPMN's default sequence flow, and the default case of a CACAO switch-condition. The Transition leaves this Step (its stonework:fromStep is this Step) and carries no guard of its own: it is the otherwise branch, so a plan doesn't have to spell out the negation of every other guard. It applies to either stonework:splitKind: with a parallel split, the default is taken only when none of the guarded branches is.

definition.value: Relates a vulnerability to a product version known to be affected by it.

scopeNote.value: The range is a stonework:VersionedProduct individual whose IRI is derived deterministically from the CPE identifier. The product individual may be populated by a separate CPE ingest; references from CVE data precede that ingest and are resolved when CPE data is loaded.

definition.value: Relates a vulnerability to the numbering authority that assigned its primary vulnerability identifier.

scopeNote.value: Resolve source-native names, UUIDs, or email addresses to an Agent individual. Like stonework:vulnerabilityId and stonework:dateAssigned, this property describes the vulnerability record's single primary identifier; represent independently assigned identifiers as distinct vulnerability records. The unresolved source string is preserved separately on cve:assigner regardless of whether resolution succeeds.

definition.value: The currency in which a normalized monetary metric value is expressed.

scopeNote.value: Required for a stonework:MetricObservation whose stonework:metricType is stonework:metricNormalizedValue. The source amount retains its own stonework:currency; this property identifies the output unit produced by the cited exchange-rate source.

definition.value: Initial delivery Infrastructure for this MalwareSample. Semantically distinct from stonework:communicatesWith, which models C2 channels post-infection.
The date and time at which a CyberActivity began.
The name of the operating system running on the host (e.g. Windows, Linux, macOS).
The individual a Hypothesis predicts its stonework:predictsVariable will be bound to, once executed.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors stonework:boundTo on the actual-result side; usable only when a specific pre-existing individual is predicted. See stonework:predictedType for the more common case of predicting a class of outcome rather than a specific not-yet-constructed individual, and stonework:predictedLiteral for predictions of a scalar.

definition.value: The monetary amount credited to the beneficiary account as this transaction's output.

scopeNote.value: Use with stonework:originatorMonetaryValue when a transaction changes denomination, as in a currency exchange. Both properties remain queryable through their stonework:hasMonetaryValue superproperty.

definition.value: Whether a MailboxRule is enabled, as last recorded.
The username or account identifier on the target system or service.
A CourseOfAction prescribes a defensive response to this AttackPattern.
The class a Hypothesis predicts its stonework:predictsVariable will be bound to an instance of, once executed.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors stonework:guardType on Transition. Exists because a Hypothesis is typically formed before the Variable's eventual value has been constructed — at prediction time there is usually no individual yet to name via stonework:predictedValue, only an expected class of outcome (e.g. 'this attempt will produce some stonework:SecurityCondition').

definition.value: Relates a Certificate to the Certificate Authority that issued it.
The on-chain address string (e.g. a Bitcoin or Ethereum address).

scopeNote.value: Resolve the address's asset through ^stonework:hasIdentifier/stonework:accountCurrency and then its ledger through stonework:blockchainNetwork on a stonework:CryptoAsset. Do not rely on the address string alone to identify the asset or network.

definition.value: Links an Incident to a Campaign it is part of or attributed to.
The Agent that holds this Account, or to whom it is beneficially attributed. Inverse of stonework:hasAccount.

scopeNote.value: For a UserAccount this is the account holder; for a FinancialAccount it is the accountholder or beneficial owner, which may differ from whoever operates it (an account-takeover attacker operating a victim's FinancialAccount is modeled with stonework:controls from the attacker-held UserAccount, leaving accountOf pointing at the victim).

definition.value: Links an Event to the raw record from which it was derived: a log, network traffic, or another artifact such as an EmailMessage whose Received headers record its route.

scopeNote.value: The Event keeps this link when an analyst later assigns it to a Step (stonework:correspondsToStep), so an execution found in evidence stays traceable to the record it came from. Name the record within the artifact with stonework:externalId on the Event, such as an audit-log record's identifier.

definition.value: An EmailAddress associated with this Agent.
The ISO 3166-2 region code (e.g. US-CA, GB-ENG).
The monetary amount debited from the originator account as this transaction's input.

scopeNote.value: Use with stonework:beneficiaryMonetaryValue when a transaction changes denomination, as in a currency exchange. Both properties remain queryable through their stonework:hasMonetaryValue superproperty.

definition.value: The Variable whose eventual binding a Hypothesis is a prediction about.

scopeNote.value: Because stonework:hasInputVariable/stonework:hasOutputVariable are declared on stonework:Behavior, and stonework:Step is itself a Behavior, a Hypothesis may predict a Variable declared at any level of a Step/Plan decomposition — a top-level Plan's overall outcome or a single Step's individual result — without a separate property per level.

definition.value: The server that performed an authentication check and recorded its result (the authserv-id of an Authentication-Results header).
The NetworkService this traffic addresses.

scopeNote.value: ⚑ Category: service *type* (HTTP, SSH, RDP, SMB, DNS) is better expressed as stonework:categorizedBy → Category named individual than as subclasses of NetworkService. NetworkService as a class is appropriate only when the instance has its own properties (port, vulnerability linkage).

definition.value: The headline context-neutral CVSS base score for this vulnerability, on a 0.0–10.0 scale.

scopeNote.value: When multiple CVSS versions are present, this SHOULD reflect the highest available version (CVSS 4.0 preferred over 3.1, 3.1 over 2.0). For full structured metric data across all CVSS versions use stonework:hasCvssMetric.

definition.value: The entity this URI serves as a locator or persistent identifier for.
The full command line string used to launch the process.
The qualitative severity corresponding to a structured CVSS assessment's base score.

scopeNote.value: cve:baseSeverity (on cve:CvssMetric) is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: Identifies the resource in the object or target position of a qualified assertion.

scopeNote.value: Range is intentionally unset because framework relationships may target either a CyberEntity, a CyberActivity, or another externally defined resource.

definition.value: Relates malware or a product to a Technique embodied by its behavior or capabilities.

scopeNote.value: Specializes the open STIX-compatible stonework:uses relationship for malware- or product-to-technique assertions. Product covers abstract product families, including Tool; VersionedProduct covers specific releases or builds. stonework:implements remains the distinct Behavior-to-Behavior realization relationship.

definition.value: An earlier EmailMessage of the same thread, named by its Message-ID in the References header.
The full URI string conforming to RFC 3986.
The security baseline(s) in which this control is required (e.g. Low, Moderate, High for NIST 800-53).
The EPSS (Exploit Prediction Scoring System) score (0.0–1.0), estimating the probability of exploitation in the wild within 30 days.

scopeNote.value: Convenience projection for a current score. Preserve dated values, source, and EPSS model version with stonework:MetricObservation and stonework:metricEpssScore.

definition.value: The date and time at which this vulnerability was publicly disclosed.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.datePublished in CVE JSON 5.x and equivalent disclosure timestamps from other vulnerability sources. cve:datePublic is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property (one-way).

definition.value: An integer score from 0 to 100 representing confidence in the accuracy of an assertion or the expected outcome of a Hypothesis.

scopeNote.value: Domain is intentionally unset because the property is shared by Hypotheses and STIX-derived intelligence objects. Matches the STIX 2.1 confidence scale for round-tripping. For source- and time-qualified confidence history, use stonework:MetricObservation with stonework:metricConfidence.

definition.value: Relates a Host to the RuntimeProcesses executing on it.
The time in an EmailMessage's Date header.

scopeNote.value: The sending client sets the Date header, so this is the sender's claim. The times receiving servers observed are on the Received hops, each a stonework:Event generatedFrom the message.

definition.value: The execution in which a VariableBinding's value was bound: the execution of the Step that outputs the Variable, or the run itself for an input supplied when it starts.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors prov:wasGeneratedBy. The run a binding belongs to is the execution it is boundIn, or the one that execution is stonework:partOfExecution, at any depth.

definition.value: Reference to the Markings applied by this marking entry.
The entity whose value is recorded by a MetricObservation.
Relates a Step to another Step that must occur before it within the same parent Behavior.

scopeNote.value: Deliberately distinct from stonework:precedes, whose domain and range are IntelligenceProduct (report-version succession) — an unrelated relationship. precededByStep expresses a graph that may contain cycles: an edge targeting an already-reached Step is a loop, not an error. A Step with several precededByStep values follows all of them; Steps with no precededByStep path between them are unordered and may be performed in parallel, so a dependency graph of precededByStep edges expresses parallel work without stonework:splitKind or stonework:joinKind. Use stonework:Transition instead when the edge itself needs a guard condition or other structure attached.

definition.value: Declares a Variable whose value is bound only once the Behavior or Step has executed.
The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, CN, RU).
A cyber activity whose occurrence prompted or provides the context for this financial transaction, without asserting that the transaction financed the activity.

scopeNote.value: Use for a victim's ransom payment linked to the incident it responds to, restitution or remediation payments, and similar contextual relationships. Use stonework:fundsActivity only when the transaction finances the linked activity.

definition.value: The total number of packets observed in the traffic flow.
Relates a threat actor to an assessment of the organizational resources available to it.
Relates a specific malware sample to the malware family it has been classified as belonging to, based on shared behavioral patterns, code similarity, infrastructure overlap, or analyst attribution.
Relates a vulnerability or an individual exploit to its exploit maturity.

scopeNote.value: At most one per subject (stonework:ExploitMaturityShape). On a vulnerability it is a convenience projection: the highest maturity currently known for it, where weaponized ranks above poc. An exploit reference, such as a stonework:OnlineReference or stonework:Tool, carries that exploit's own maturity. Domain is unset so each of these subjects is valid. Dated history is not recorded on this property.

definition.value: A Role whose holder is expected to perform this Step: the plan-side assignment of work, as in a BPMN lane.

scopeNote.value: If several Roles are given, a holder of any one of them may perform the Step; a requirement that two people act (dual control) is two Steps, linked by stonework:separatedFrom. An execution conforms when its performer, or the Agent its performer identity belongs to (stonework:accountOf, stonework:attributedToAgent), holds the Role through a stonework:RoleAssignment whose stonework:roleContext is the Plan's performer and which is in force (stonework:validFrom, stonework:validUntil) when the execution starts. Someone acting through a role holder's misused identity passes this check, which is why a misused identity is recorded as a stonework:Deviation.

definition.value: An address in an EmailMessage's Cc header.
Relates a ThreatScenario to the AttackTechniques in the attack path.
Relates a Procedure to the Technique it implements; a specialized form of stonework:implements for procedure-to-technique links.
Indicates two entities share common attributes, infrastructure, or behaviour, suggesting possible connection without asserting a specific relationship type.
Relates a Report or Sighting to the Agent who created it.
Relates an Investigation to the Investigation it was merged into, once analysts concluded the two examine the same matter.

scopeNote.value: Keeps the merged Investigation as a record rather than deleting it, so its identity, findings and history stay traceable. A merge is an analyst's decision; when and by whom are recorded through stonework:hasProvenance or a stonework:QualifiedAssertion.

definition.value: Relates a malware sample or family to one or more functional type classifications.

scopeNote.value: A malware sample may have multiple types (e.g. a trojan that also acts as a downloader). Aligns with the STIX 2.1 malware-type open vocabulary.

definition.value: Relates a DigitalArtifact to the Host on which it is stored.
Relates a threat actor to an assessment of its technical sophistication.
The fully qualified domain name string (e.g. malicious-site.com).
Shortcut triple: generic relationship. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'related-to'.
Relates an IntelligenceProduct or QualifiedAssertion to a Provenance record documenting its origin or evidentiary basis.
The literal value that guardVariable's bound value is compared against.

scopeNote.value: Compared using the operator given by stonework:guardOperator; if guardOperator is omitted, comparison defaults to Equals. Must share a compatible, numerically-typed datatype with the guardVariable's stonework:boundToLiteral value when an ordering operator is used.

definition.value: Relates a product family to a specific versioned product instance.
Relates a transaction, account, or impact to a stonework:MonetaryAmount stating a sum of money and its currency.
Links any individual to one or more contextual categories.

scopeNote.value: This is the primary mechanism for flexible, context-sensitive classification (e.g., Evidence, HighValue, Suspect, etc.). Multiple categories per individual are allowed.

definition.value: Relates a Campaign or Operation to an Agent that conducts it.
Relates an entity to a Group, Organization, or ThreatActor to which it belongs.
Relates a DataAsset or Infrastructure to its owning Agent.
Relates an Incident to an Event that forms part of its recorded activity.
Relates an Agent to a product family it develops or maintains.
Relates infrastructure or a product version to known Vulnerabilities it contains.
Relates a threat actor to one or more classifications describing their organizational form or primary mode of operation.

scopeNote.value: A threat actor may have multiple types (e.g. nation-state actor who is also a spy). Aligns with the STIX 2.1 threat-actor-type open vocabulary.

definition.value: Associates any object with an OnlineReference (blog post, advisory URL, disclosure, vendor bulletin). Primary arc into the OnlineReference class.
The date the domain registration expires.
Relates a Log or NetworkTraffic to the system that produced it.
The CWE abstraction level: Pillar, Class, Base, or Variant.
Relates a File, MalwareSample, or Tool to another File, MalwareSample, or Tool it retrieves during execution.
Relates a Location to a broader Location that wholly contains it, e.g. a City to its Region or Country, or a Region to its Country.

scopeNote.value: Transitive: a City locatedWithin a Region that is locatedWithin a Country is also locatedWithin that Country. Assert only the most direct containment and let reasoning supply the rest. Use stonework:locatedAt to place non-Location entities such as Hosts or Organizations at a Location.

definition.value: The name string of the mutex object.
The Package URL (PURL) identifying this software package version.
An address in an EmailMessage's To header.
The IBAN string, including country prefix and check digits.
An optional ordinal position for a Step within a strictly linear Behavior, where the full precededByStep graph is unnecessary.

scopeNote.value: Most CTI procedure write-ups (a numbered list of adversary actions) are linear. stepOrder is a low-overhead alternative to precededByStep for that common case; the two are not mutually exclusive.

definition.value: The Subject header of an EmailMessage.
Relates a weakness to the vulnerability that exploits or instantiates it.

scopeNote.value: The range is a vulnerability individual. The weakness individual (domain) is a stonework:Weakness whose IRI is derived from the CWE identifier. The weakness individual may be populated by a separate CWE ingest.
